title: Gedi (Gede) ruins
summary: Gede (Gedi) was a Swahili trading town on the Kenyan coast, founded between the early 12th and early 14th centuries depending on the source, and flourishing in the 14th and 15th centuries. Its houses, mosques and tombs yielded imported goods such as Venetian beads and a Ming vase. It was abandoned in the early 17th century.

uncertainty.note: Founding is "early 12th century" on one page and "late 13th or early 14th century" on another; start year 1125 is the earlier reading, with the plus range reaching 1300. Abandonment is "the beginning of the 17th century" or "the early 17th century"; one page also says "early 16th century" elsewhere in its text.
